question: A science book depicts magnetic field lines around two bar magnets marked A and B. From A, five lines emerge from its north pole, and in B, ten lines enter into its south pole. The strength of A is _______ that of B.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Half**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Given the information: **Magnet A has 5 field lines** emerging from its north pole.
 
• **Magnet B has 10 field lines** entering into its south pole
 
• .To compare the strength of magnet A to magnet B: The strength of magnet A can be represented as 5 (since it has 5 lines).
 
• The strength of magnet B can be represented as 10 (since it has 10 lines).
 
• The strength of magnet A relative to magnet B can be calculated as follows: **Strength of A =10/5 = 1/2** ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic field lines are visual representations** of the magnetic field around a magnet or a current-carrying conductor.
 
• Magnetic field lines emerge from the **north pole of a magnet and enter through the south pole**.
 
• The density of the magnetic field lines represents the **strength of the magnetic field. **
 
• A bar magnet shows a uniform magnetic field around it.
 
• The **Earth itself has a magnetic field**, which can be represented by field lines that **extend from the magnetic north pole to the magnetic south pole**, influencing compasses and navigation.
